4. As many as 26 the plaintiffs have been separately enjoying and possessing the suit land by erecting different shops over their own portion for the last 12 years. The defendants bad no right, title, possession and interest over the suit land and C.S, S.A. and B.S. khatians were prepared and recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and their predecessors and they have been paying rent to the Government regularly. The defendants threatened to demolish the plaintiffs' shops and to dispossess them from the suit land on 25.11.2002 on the basis of notices dated 24.11.2002 as described in the second schedule to the plaint and therefore, the plaintiffs filed the instant suit. 

 5. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint of the suit. Their case, in short, is that the suit is bad for defect of parties and it is also barred by limitation. The suit land was under khash possession of Radha Kishore and he did not give any settlement of this land. Pursuant to the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the then Government of Pakistan became the owner of the suit land. During the preparation of the S.A. khatian, the suit land was not recorded in the name of the Government because of carelessness and negligence of Survey Department as well as Roads and Highways Department. The suit land was illegally recorded in the names of different persons who are the vendors or transferors of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs are not entitled to get a decree as prayed for. On different occasions, Roads and Highways Department requested the plaintiffs to leave the premises but they failed to vacate the premises. On 24.11.2002, the defendants served notices upon the plain-tiffs to show cause as to why they would not be evicted from the suit land. Therefore, the notices were not illegal. For the reasons stated, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 14. The High Court Division found that the plaintiffs had been able to prove their prima-facie title to the suit land by producing the papers of settlement from the sherista of the Zaminder. The High Court Division further found that S.A. and B.S. khatians were prepared in the names of the plaintiffs and that they also produced rent receipts sowing payment of rent which proved that the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession of the suit land. The High Court Division noted that exhibit-3 series, the notices issued upon the plaintiffs proved that the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession of the suit land. The High Court Division came to a finding that the suit land had been properly described in the schedule to the plaint and that there was no vagueness in the description of the suit land.
